headline: Urgent: ER or hospital risk 6% in the next 7 days, about 5x usual
summary: Urgent: risk of an ER visit or hospital admission in the next 7 days is 6% (urgent line 6%, typical day 1.2%). Risk of a rough patch in the next 7 days: 16% (alert line 11%). The treatment calendar alone gives 9%; wearable signals move it +7 points. Biggest wearable driver: Sleep efficiency 87% vs usual 92%, waking 3.5x a night vs 2.0x, 6.8 h asleep vs 7.1 h.

profile.context: Day 5 of cycle 4 (IV chemo every 21 days)

evidence.label: Sleep
evidence.text: Sleep efficiency 87% vs usual 92%, waking 3.5x a night vs 2.0x, 6.8 h asleep vs 7.1 h

evidence.label: Steps
evidence.text: Steps 38% below their usual (7,721 vs 12,395 a day, last 3 days)

evidence.label: Heart rate variability
evidence.text: Heart rate variability 26% lower than usual (recovery down)

evidence.label: Check-ins
evidence.unit: daily check-ins skipped in a row
evidence.text: Skipped the last 3 daily check-ins. Across the program, people who come back after 3+ skips report a rough day 1.4x as often; today's wearable estimate: 13% chance today is rough (typical 6%)

evidence.label: Treatment calendar
evidence.text: Day 5 of cycle 4 (IV chemo every 21 days). The calendar alone predicts 9% risk of a rough patch this week.

recommendations.action: Call today. Ask how they feel, about fever, fluids and anything new. If anything is off, have them call their care team now.
recommendations.why: Their wearable pattern matches the days before an ER visit or hospital stay. The coach does not diagnose; the care team decides.

recommendations.action: Check in this week about sleep: nights, naps, worries. Share the sleep tips sheet.
recommendations.why: Sleep got shorter or more broken than usual.

recommendations.action: Move the next coaching call earlier and plan around the expected low point.
recommendations.why: The forecast covers the next 7 days.

recommendations.action: Send a short, no-pressure message asking how the week is going; offer a 2-minute call instead of the form.
recommendations.why: 3 daily check-ins skipped in a row; rough days are more common after a run of skips.
